text:
Anya: quick idea — want to propose a streaming TF/PT -> safetensors transcode adapter in the loader layer. goal: let hosted + dedicated runtimes accept legacy checkpoints without a heavy offline rewrite. adapter would stream-convert tensors, emit safetensors frames, and support partial-range reads for warmup. thoughts? :thinking:
Devon: sounds neat. main worry is CPU + memory blowup on high-qps paths. where does conversion happen? worker side or prefetcher?
Anya: conversion would be colocated in the weights-loader process (not the GPU infer worker). workflow: 1) receive request to open a bundle, 2) if bundle format != safetensors, spawn streaming transcoder that reads source and emits safetensors chunks to a sharded cache, and 3) loader presents a safetensors-like interface to upper layers, with lazy emit for ranges used by warmup.
Ravi: two questions: checksum/signing semantics (we currently trust safetensors header + index). how do we preserve provenance when we transcode on the fly? and second: what about memory pinning for the converted backing store?
Anya: good call. plan is to generate a conversion manifest with: original digest, converter version, and produced safetensors digest. manifest gets signed by the conversion service's key and stored alongside converted shards in our ephemeral object store. loader will validate the signed-manifest before exposing data.
Jules: how do we avoid repeated conversions of the same upstream artifact? we need a deterministic cache key.
Anya: deterministic key = sha256(original-artifact) + converter-semver + quant-profile-id + target-endianness. if key hits, we reuse converted shards (and their manifest). eviction TTL backed by storage LRU.
Devon: what about partial reads? warmup should be able to ask for first N layers without forcing full conversion. can the adapter lazily transcode ranges?
Anya: yes — design is range-driven streaming: the transcoder reads only requested tensor byte ranges (plus small alignment slack) and emits completed safetensors chunks for those ranges. we maintain an append-only chunk index so subsequent reads can reuse produced bytes.
Ravi: this still sounds I/O heavy. we should throttle conversion concurrency and prioritize warmup ranges vs cold full conversions. also add a fast-path: if the source is already memmap-friendly (tf checkpoint with contiguous tensors), we can zero-copy map+wrap instead of reserialize.
Jules: compatibility: some PT pickles include GPU tensors and strange dtypes. converter must sanitize dtype mapping and optionally apply a safe-quant profile (fp16 -> int8 plan) with explicit metadata. need an opt-in policy — we can't silently change weights.
Anya: agreed. default is lossless transform (float32 -> float32). quant/transcode is opt-in per workload via model spec. manifest records any lossy transforms and quant profiles used.
Devon: telemetry: we need histograms for conversion latency, CPU seconds per conversion, bytes emitted, and fraction of warmup hits satisfied by lazy ranges. also an alert if conversion time > X s for hot models.
Anya: will add metrics hooks. also thinking about operator UX: a CLI to prewarm and pin converted artifacts: `rw convert --src s3://... --target safetensors --pin` which writes to our shared cache.
loader-bot: conversion task started: task_id=conv-2026-03-10-421, src=gs://modelz/legacy/v3.ckpt, node=conv-03
Ravi: rollout plan: start as opt-in flag on dedicated clusters; run converter as sidecar and enable prewarm CLI for customers migrating. collect perf for 2 weeks before enabling on hosted.
Jules: post-mortem/hardening: add fuzz tests for corrupted pt headers and malformed tensor shapes; ensure converter never exposes partially-written chunks without manifest signature.
Anya: perf probe we should run: convert a 10B RoBERTa-style checkpoint, request 2 first transformer blocks as warmup, measure time to first-token on hosted vs baseline offline-convert+serve. aim: <= 2x offline conversion cold latency for first-token with much less storage ops.
Devon: ok — create a short RFC PR describing interface boundaries (Loader <-> Transcoder API), manifest schema, cache key spec, and throttling defaults. I'll review tomorrow. :+1:
Anya: thanks — I'll draft the RFC and include pseudocode for the streaming API and a small ascii diagram of chunk index layout.
Jules: LGTM in principle. small nit: ensure KMS integration for manifest signing keys and a clear revoke/rotate story.
Anya: noted. will add KMS rotation section. thanks everyone! :tada:
